description: We are a dynamic and highly motivated tech team passionate about building visually striking and functionally robust applications. Led by Eyad Ramy, who specializes in web development and creative 2D design, our core philosophy is bridging the gap between beautiful aesthetics and solid code to create engaging user experiences. We are joined by a talented roster of developers and problem-solvers: Omar Ahmed, Omar Ehab, Adham Ashraf, and Elhussein Mostafa.
summary: **Where They Rest** is an interactive, museum-style web monograph designed for learners ages 9 to 14 that explores the silent afterlife of NASA’s greatest off-world spacecraft. Across five structured chapters, readers journey from Earth to the Moon, Mars, and deep space to uncover the science and engineering behind four iconic explorers: the **Apollo 11 Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector**, the **Opportunity** rover, the **Ingenuity** helicopter, and the **Kepler Space Telescope**. Combining verified NASA archival plates, authentic mission telemetry, and interactive 3D CAD models with exploded parts set in their planetary environments, it turns retired machines into enduring monuments of human curiosity.
details:
Chapter I · Silent Monuments (Overview & Earthrise)

  • Archival Plate: NASA / Apollo 8 Crew (William Anders), Earthrise (AS08-14-2383), photographed from lunar orbit on December 24, 1968. NASA Johnson Space Center / NASA Image and Video Library.
  • Mission Reference: NASA History Division & NASA Science, Apollo 8 Mission Overview and Lunar Orbital Telemetry.

Chapter II · Apollo 11 Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR)

  • Archival Plate: NASA / Apollo 11 Crew (Neil Armstrong), Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector Deployed at Tranquility Base (AS11-40-5952), Sea of Tranquility, Moon, July 21, 1969. NASA Johnson Space Center.
  • Spacecraft & Instrument Record: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), Apollo 11 Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package (EASEP) — Laser Ranging Retroreflector (Catalog ID: 1969-059C-04).
  • Scientific Telemetry: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center & Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), Lunar Laser Ranging (LLR) Earth–Moon Recession (+3.8 cm/year), Lunar Core Structure, and General Relativity Verification Data.

Chapter III · Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity (MER-B)

  • Archival Plate: NASA / JPL-Caltech / Cornell University / Arizona State University (ASU), Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity Panoramic Camera (Pancam) & Navigation Camera (Navcam) Imagery (Eagle Crater, Meridiani Planum, and Endeavour Crater, 2004–2018).
  • Spacecraft & Mission Record: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) / NSSDCA, Mars Exploration Rover-B (Opportunity) (Catalog ID: 2003-032A), Meridiani Planum Landing Archive (January 25, 2004) and End-of-Mission Summary Report (February 13, 2019).
  • Scientific Telemetry: NASA Mars Exploration Program, Hematite ("Blueberry") Concretion Findings, 45.16 km Odometer Log, and June 2018 Global Dust Storm Telemetry.

Chapter IV · Ingenuity Mars Helicopter

  • Archival Plate: NASA / JPL-Caltech / Arizona State University (ASU) / Malin Space Science Systems (MSSS), Mars 2020 Perseverance Mastcam-Z & Ingenuity Navigation Camera Imagery (Wright Brothers Field and Valinor Hills, Jezero Crater, 2021–2024).
  • Spacecraft & Mission Record: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) / NSSDCA, Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Technology Demonstration (Catalog ID: 2020-052A), First Powered Flight Log (April 19, 2021) and Flight 72 End-of-Mission Report (January 18, 2024).
  • Engineering Telemetry: NASA/JPL Mars Helicopter Team, Counter-Rotating Carbon-Fiber Rotor Specifications (2,400–2,537 RPM) and 72-Flight Distance & Altitude Records.

Chapter V · Kepler Space Telescope

  • Archival Plate & Diagrams: NASA Ames Research Center / JPL-Caltech, Kepler Space Telescope Spacecraft Renderings & Cygnus–Lyra Field-of-View Photometry Plates.
  • Spacecraft & Mission Record: NASA Ames Research Center / NSSDCA, Kepler Space Telescope (Catalog ID: 2009-011A), Launch & Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit Telemetry (March 7, 2009 – October 30, 2018).
  • Exoplanet Discovery Data: NASA Exoplanet Archive (Caltech / IPAC), First Five Exoplanets Announcement (Kepler-4b, 5b, 6b, 7b, and 8b — January 4, 2010), Kepler-11 Six-Planet System Confirmation (February 2, 2011), and Kepler & K2 Confirmed Exoplanet Catalog.
